items.title: PNGRB proposes 14% assured returns to attract investment in natural gas pipelines

items.title: Pioneer brewer of the Nilgiris remembered
points: The Nilgiri Documentation Centre (NDC) remembered a “pioneer brewer of The Nilgiris” at his grave in All Saints Church, Coonoor, recently to mark World Heritage Week.
The brewer, Samuel Honeywell, is said to have died in February of 1891 and is buried with his wife and two children.
Venugopal Dharmalingam, honorary director of the NDC, said that Honeywell was the first to start a brewery in the Nilgiris in 1857 at Aravankadu, which he called the Castle Brewery.
He also established retail shops in Ooty, Kandal, Coonoor and Kotagiri, Burliar & Wellington.

More breweries are said to have followed Honeywell’s venture including one in 1872, when Captain Albert started the Llangollen Brewery near Marliamund that failed to meet the required standards and was closed in 1883.
In 1879, the Nilgiri Brewery, one of the biggest on the hills, was started by the Murree Brewery Company from Himachal Pradesh.
In 1895, the Rose and Crown Brewery was started at Yellanalli by Muni Huchanna.

items.title: 3 die while cleaning septic tank in Hyderabad; probe underway: Police

“The workers entered the underground septic tank to clean it but did not come out.

items.title: How chokepoint disruption reshapes maritime risk
points: Around 90% of world trade travels by sea, much of it through a relatively small number of narrow maritime passages.
Ships wait, divert or change schedules, with the effects often reaching far beyond the original point of disruption.
Recent Pole Star Global research, using Pole Star Global Zone Traffic data from nine major chokepoints between January 2024 and September 2026, gives a sense of the scale.
Among the clearest shifts, average daily transits through the Strait of Hormuz were 64.9% lower between January and August 2026, than over the same period in 2024.
Bosporus Strait traffic rose by 176.5% on the same comparison, while Panama Canal traffic was 28.2% higher.

Saleem Khan, Chief Data & Analytics Officer, Pole Star Global, explains why a wider view of maritime risk is becoming increasingly important for operators and insurers navigating a more volatile trading environment.
Daily transits averaged 27.5 in 2024, during the El Niño drought restrictions, before recovering to more than 35 in 2026.

points: Copper futures fell to around $5.50 per pound on Tuesday, resuming their downward trend toward eight-month lows as the broad metals rally in the previous session, driven by Jensen Huang’s return as Nvidia CEO, lost momentum.
The metal remained under pressure from uncertainty surrounding artificial intelligence investment, subdued Chinese demand and expectations of further US Federal Reserve rate hikes.

items.title: European Gas Prices Rise Further Amid Winter Supply Fears
points: European natural gas prices rose past €90/MWh on Tuesday after reaching an intraday high of €96/MWh on Monday, as forecasts of a cold spell intensified concerns over the region’s already strained gas supply.
The latest forecasts point to colder-than-normal conditions across Northwest Europe that would persist into early December, which could drive up heating demand and accelerate storage withdrawals.

Adding to this, forecasts of weaker wind speeds across Germany, the Netherlands and Denmark in the middle of the week could reduce wind power generation, potentially prompting producers to increase gas-fired output to compensate for the shortfall.
Europe’s gas storage sites were less than 69% full, well below seasonal averages, leaving the region with a limited buffer against extreme winter cold and further supply shocks.
Temperatures are also expected to fall below seasonal norms in parts of Asia in the coming days, potentially intensifying competition for available LNG cargoes.

items.title: European shares pause after month-best rally on Nvidia euphoria
points: European equities paused for breath on Tuesday, edging marginally lower as investors digested a historic, Nvidia-fueled relief rally and pivoted their focus back to a formidable U.S. monetary policy overhang.
The pan-European STOXX 600 index was unchanged in morning dealing, consolidating after logging a 1.7% jump – its best single-session performance in nearly a month on Monday.
Germany’s DAX fell 0.3%, while France’s CAC 40 was up 0.2%.
The catalyst behind the sudden revival in global risk appetite was the reappointment of Jensen Huang as Nvidia’s chief executive.
Shares of the U.S. chipmaker rocketed 31.5% on Monday – marking their biggest daily percentage gain in 23 years – and restoring nearly $1 trillion in market value in a single session.

Allocators are squarely focused on Wednesday’s release of the U.S. Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) price index, the Federal Reserve’s preferred inflation gauge, which arrives ahead of the central bank’s final policy meeting of 2026.

items.title: North Sea decommissioning spending set to hit $32bn by 2035
points: Oil and gas companies operating in the UK North Sea are expected to spend £24.7bn ($32.5bn) on decommissioning over the next decade, according to a new report from industry body Offshore Energies UK (OEUK).
The organisation’s latest decommissioning outlook forecasts expenditure between 2026 and 2035, with annual spending expected to peak at approximately £3.1bn ($4bn) in 2027.
Spending is projected to remain above £2.7bn ($3.52bn) annually through 2031 as operators proceed with well abandonment, platform removal, and subsea infrastructure recovery.
The programme includes decommissioning 1,834 wells and removing 135 platform topsides and 126 subsea structures.
The central North Sea is expected to account for approximately 56% of total expenditure during the period.

The organisation expects new UK offshore wind capacity additions to peak at around 5.2GW in 2029, increasing pressure on some of the same marine construction and installation resources required for decommissioning.

items.title: Changing of the guard at Samsung Heavy
points: South Korea’s Samsung Heavy Industries has named chief operating officer Lee Wang-geun as its next president and CEO, succeeding vice chairman Choi Sung-an.

He has served as COO and head of the group’s shipbuilding and offshore division since late 2025.

In 2016, India and Nepal agreed to establish an Eminent Persons Group to look at the entire relationship between the two countries.
One of the main areas of its study was the Treaty of Peace and Friendship in 1950.
The report provided an opportunity for Nepal to relook at the 1950 treaty, security cooperation, the open border and the overall balance of the relationship.

items.title: Email threatens bomb blast at Diljit Dosanjh’s Bengaluru concert venue, case filed

“The scale of government borrowing today is larger, and so is the importance of the market-making role that the PDs play,” Jain said at the Primary Dealers’ Association of India Seminar 2026 in Mumbai on Monday.

items.title: 5G Not Working on Your Phone? How to Fix Network and Settings Problems

items.title: Toll Plazas Will Automatically Check PUC, Insurance, RC; And Automatically Fine You For Invalid Documents
points: Driving through a highway toll plaza in Gujarat could now lead to a traffic challan even if a police officer never stops your car.
The state is extending its electronic document-checking system to private cars and two-wheelers.
Cameras at toll plazas will read registration numbers, check official databases and flag vehicles whose mandatory documents have expired or are invalid.
The system was previously used mainly for commercial vehicles such as trucks and buses.
Private motorists are now being brought within its scope.
The transport department has asked owners to check three documents in particular: their Pollution Under Control (PUC) certificate, motor insurance and registration certificate (RC).
A camera at a toll plaza captures the vehicle's number plate.
Passing through a toll gate does not mean a driver has agreed to a new fee, and the state has not announced a special new fine merely for using the highway.

items.title: NHAI To Bust Bad Contractors Using Dashcams: 50,000 Kms Of Highways Under Watch
points: A dangerous pothole or a missing road marking can remain on a highway for days even after thousands of vehicles have driven over it.
The National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) wants to make it much harder for maintenance contractors to ignore such problems.
It has brought nearly 50,000 km of national highways under a dashcam-based monitoring system that identifies defects, records where they are and sends evidence to the people responsible for repairs.
The next step is to calculate penalties automatically when contractors miss their deadlines.
Software then looks for around 40 types of problems, including potholes, faded lane markings, rutting, damaged surfaces, defective lighting and unsafe work zones.
According to data reported by The Times of India, the system detected 92,088 defects in roughly two months of its initial rollout.
About 23 per cent related to faded road markings and about 15 per cent to potholes.
Roughly 72 per cent had been rectified, while around 17 per cent were overdue.

items.title: SEBI issues upcoming IPOs GMP advisory - ‘publication of such pre-listing premium figures may be detrimental’
points: The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) has stepped up its scrutiny of the unofficial grey market surrounding initial public offerings (IPOs), asking market intermediaries and participants to discontinue the publication and circulation of grey…
In an advisory issued on Monday, 23 November, the market regulator cautioned investors against relying on GMP as an indication of an IPO's likely listing price or expected returns.
The move comes amid the widespread circulation of IPO GMP figures across websites, digital platforms, newspapers and social media.
The regulator described GMP as unofficial and unverified prices at which shares are supposedly traded before their formal listing on a recognised stock exchange.

In its statement, SEBI said the publication, display, circulation or dissemination of such unregulated pre-listing premiums through any mode or platform may be discontinued across the securities market.

It specifically advised all SEBI-registered intermediaries and market participants to refrain from publishing, displaying or broadcasting GMP figures on their websites, platforms or through other communication channels, including emails, SMS and social media.
